name: Hugh Taylor Birch State Park
dates: Year-round, daily 8 a.m. to sunset; ranger walks Friday and Saturday
customer: Walkers, birders, paddlers, cyclists, beach visitors
unique: Hugh Taylor Birch's former 180-acre Terramar estate preserves maritime hammock, coastal dune lakes and a 1.9-mile park drive between the Intracoastal Waterway and the ocean.
buzz: The contrast with the surrounding beach development is the draw. Friday and Saturday ranger walks are included with admission. The floating dock has been closed since May 11, 2026, so check current paddling access.

name: Historic Stranahan House Museum
dates: Year-round, 5–6 days weekly; daily audio tours and advance-arranged docent tours
customer: History readers, architecture visitors, first-time Fort Lauderdale visitors
unique: Frank and Ivy Stranahan's 1901 New River house preserves the trading post, ferry crossing and community rooms around which Fort Lauderdale developed, with the family's furnishings and personal history in the rooms.
buzz: The house is small and the family story carries the visit. Daily admission uses a 45-minute audio wand. Weekly availability changes with school groups and rentals, and ghost tours have been discontinued permanently.

name: Museum of Discovery and Science
dates: Year-round; Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday noon–5 p.m.
customer: Families, science visitors, curious adults, rainy-day travelers
unique: Two floors combine Florida ecosystems and live animal ambassadors with aviation, engineering, a makerspace, live science demonstrations and the large-format AutoNation IMAX theater.
buzz: The scheduled animal encounters, KaBoom demonstrations and makerspace activities reward checking the daily calendar rather than wandering without a plan. Combination tickets can include HoloTheater and an IMAX documentary.

name: NSU Art Museum Fort Lauderdale
dates: Year-round; Tuesday–Saturday 11 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closed Monday
customer: Art museum visitors, modern-art readers, couples, architecture people
unique: A permanent collection of more than 7,500 works includes substantial CoBrA holdings and the largest collection of William J. Glackens's work and archives, alongside African, Oceanic and Americas art.
buzz: The Glackens and CoBrA holdings distinguish this from a general contemporary-art stop. Sunday public tours run at 2 p.m., and the first Thursday of each month is free with hours extended to 7 p.m.

name: Fort Lauderdale Water Taxi
dates: Year-round, daily 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; weather and marine traffic affect service
customer: First-time visitors, boat watchers, photographers, travelers without a car
unique: A hop-on, hop-off boat circuit through the New River and Intracoastal canals links more than 30 stops in Fort Lauderdale, Pompano Beach and Hollywood, making the working waterfront and canal neighborhoods the itinerary.
buzz: Treat the full Fort Lauderdale loop as a three-hour outing rather than punctual transportation. Boats generally arrive every 30–45 minutes, and the live tracker is useful because weather, bridge openings and boat traffic cause delays.

name: History Fort Lauderdale Museum Campus
dates: Year-round, daily 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; docent tours at 1, 2 and 3 p.m.
customer: Local-history readers, researchers, architecture visitors, families
unique: The 1905 New River Inn, 1907 Pioneer House and 1899 Ivy Cromartie Schoolhouse form a museum campus on the river, with artist studios and a research library holding photographs, maps and architectural drawings.
buzz: The guided three-museum ticket gives more context than a quick self-guided room circuit. The campus is compact, but the archival photo collection and artists-in-residence make it more than a period-house tour.

name: Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale Museum
dates: Year-round, Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; last tour 2:30 p.m.; closed major holidays
company: Naval Air Station Fort Lauderdale Museum
customer: Aviation readers, veterans, World War II visitors, families
unique: A volunteer-run museum at the wartime torpedo-bomber training base preserves letters, photographs and artifacts from Flight 19, the five Avengers that disappeared after leaving Fort Lauderdale on December 5, 1945.
buzz: The documents and volunteer knowledge are the reasons to visit, not a large aircraft collection. Hours are limited to weekends, and the Flight 19 material separates the training flight and failed search from later Bermuda Triangle mythology.

name: Old Dillard Museum
cost: Free; tours and programs by arrangement
dates: School-year tours and public programs; contact the museum for an appointment before visiting
customer: Black-history visitors, music fans, educators, local-history readers
unique: Fort Lauderdale's 1924 school for Black students now holds exhibits on education and community life, including a jazz room devoted to former Dillard teacher Julian Cannonball Adderley.
buzz: The building and the personal accounts are the substance, and visitors who get a guided tour report learning far more than the small galleries initially suggest. This is a school-district museum, so do not assume daily walk-in access.

name: Everglades Holiday Park Airboat Tour
dates: Year-round, daily from 9 a.m.; last full 60-minute tour 4 p.m.; weather and water levels affect trips
customer: First-time Everglades visitors, families, wildlife watchers
unique: A 60-minute airboat run from the Griffin Road edge of the Everglades combines sawgrass and open-water wildlife habitat with a separate alligator presentation by the park associated with the Gator Boys television series.
buzz: The boat is the reason to go and the alligator presentation is staged entertainment. Boats depart frequently, but arriving 30 minutes early matters. The last 4:30 p.m. boat is only a 30-minute ride.

name: Hollywood Hot Glass Class
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Sunday 1–9 p.m.; class booking required
customer: Maker travelers, couples, families, art students
unique: Inside ArtsPark at Young Circle, beginners work with an instructor and molten glass to shape and color a piece of their own rather than merely watching a demonstration.
buzz: The hands-on portion is about 20 minutes, so the appeal is concentrated rather than a full afternoon. Glass needs roughly 12 hours to cool, which means planning a later pickup during Wednesday-to-Sunday gallery hours.

name: Anne Kolb Nature Center and West Lake Park
cost: Free nature center; rentals and some park entrances extra
dates: Year-round; nature center daily 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; park 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; marina usually Saturday–Monday, weather permitting
customer: Birders, paddlers, photographers, families
unique: A 1,500-acre coastal mangrove estuary with marked paddling trails, a 68-foot observation tower, a 3,500-gallon aquarium and an exhibit hall explaining the ecology of West Lake.
buzz: The tower and aquarium make an easy short visit, but the mangrove trails are the fuller experience. The rental marina keeps a shorter, weather-dependent schedule than the nature center, so call before planning around a paddle.

name: Cinema Paradiso Hollywood
dates: Year-round; scheduled screenings and festival programs, check current calendar
company: Broward County Film Society and Fort Lauderdale International Film Festival
customer: Independent-film viewers, documentary audiences, couples
unique: An 82-seat downtown arthouse screens first-run independent, foreign-language and documentary films, with retrospectives and Fort Lauderdale International Film Festival programming in the same rotation.
buzz: The small room and focused programming are the appeal for viewers who do not want another multiplex screen. Showtimes are film-specific rather than continuous, and Hollywood residents get a Wednesday ticket and popcorn special.

name: Dania Beach Invitational Jai Alai
dates: Seasonal tournament; January 5–March 31, 2027, with matinees and evening sessions; verify each year's schedule
customer: Sports curious travelers, history visitors, bettors, nightlife groups
unique: Professional pelotaris use curved cestas to hurl the pelota off the three-walled court at the 1953 Dania fronton, keeping a South Florida gambling and sporting institution visible to spectators.
buzz: The speed of the ball and the rhythm of the scoring are easier to follow in the small fronton than on a stream. This is now a limited invitational season, not the old year-round schedule, and the operator notes that seats are limited.

name: Dr. Von D. Mizell-Eula Johnson State Park
dates: Year-round, daily 8 a.m. to sunset; construction and facility notices apply
customer: Beach visitors, civil-rights history readers, anglers, birders
unique: A 310-acre barrier beach beside Port Everglades preserves 2.5 miles of undeveloped coast and tells the history of the segregated beach and the wade-in campaigns led by Eula Johnson, Dr. Von D. Mizell and others.
buzz: The beach and the civil-rights history reward equal time. Port dredging and north-jetty work began in 2025 and 2026, with some work expected through early 2028, so check current access and restroom closures before a long visit.

name: Jaxson's Ice Cream Parlor and Restaurant
dates: Year-round; Sunday–Thursday 11:30 a.m.–11 p.m., Friday–Saturday until midnight; closed Thanksgiving
customer: Families, ice-cream traditionalists, roadside-food collectors
unique: Monroe Udell's family-run parlor has made ice cream on Federal Highway since 1956, with dozens of flavors and toppings, oversized sundaes and a dining room packed with old license plates and memorabilia.
buzz: The house-made ice cream and the cluttered room are the institution; the full savory menu is secondary for many visitors. Late hours make it useful after a flight or cruise, but expect a wait at peak dessert times.

name: Round Up Line Dancing Lessons
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Sunday; line-dance lesson 7:30 p.m. and couples lesson 8:30 p.m.
customer: Dance beginners, country-music fans, nightlife groups, couples
unique: Davie's country nightclub teaches a line dance and a couples dance before open dancing every operating night, giving a first-time visitor a structured way onto the floor rather than leaving them to watch regulars.
buzz: Arrive for the lessons instead of treating this as a late-night bar stop. Age rules and covers change by night, Sunday has an all-ages option, and the mechanical bull runs only on selected Thursdays.

name: Old Davie School Historical Museum
dates: Self-guided Tuesday–Friday 12:30–2:30 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; guided tours by appointment
customer: Local-history readers, school groups, architecture visitors
unique: Broward County's oldest existing school building on its original site, built in 1918, holds classrooms, artifacts and exhibits about the settlers, farms and education of early Davie and western Broward.
buzz: The original building makes the local history tangible, but public hours are narrow and morning school programming takes precedence. A guided tour requires booking at least 24 hours ahead.

name: Bergeron Rodeo Grounds
dates: Event-driven year-round; Wednesday barrel racing and rodeos on the Town of Davie calendar
customer: Rodeo first-timers, western-culture visitors, families
unique: Davie's longtime rodeo arena still anchors its western-themed downtown with professional and youth rodeos, barrel racing and the Orange Blossom Rodeo rather than presenting cowboy culture only as storefront decoration.
buzz: Choose an actual rodeo or barrel-racing date, since the grounds are otherwise an event venue. The 2026 calendar included Wednesday barrel racing, professional rodeos and the November Southeast Circuit Finals.

name: Tree Tops Park and Pine Island Ridge
cost: Free; weekend gate fee may apply
dates: Year-round, daily daylight hours; confirm current tower and boardwalk access
customer: Walkers, birders, equestrians, families
unique: Wetland boardwalks, oak hammock, horse trails and an observation tower occupy land once intended for a golf community, with the adjacent Pine Island Ridge natural area adding wooded trails.
buzz: The wetland boardwalk and purple gallinules are reliable reasons for a slow walk, while the tower is a secondary stop. Recent visitor guidance recommends asking staff about current tower and boardwalk access rather than assuming both are open.

name: Brian Piccolo Park Velodrome
cost: $25 annual individual track pass; program and event fees vary
dates: Year-round scheduled training, certification and races; check organizer calendar before visiting
company: Broward County Parks and Florida Velodrome Association
customer: Cyclists, track-racing spectators, skaters, youth athletes
unique: A 333.3-meter concrete track with banking up to about 30 degrees, a 200-meter infield warm-up track and lights supports certification, youth training, racing and inline skating in one county facility.
buzz: This is not a turn-up-on-a-road-bike attraction. Rider certification and organizer schedules matter, while spectators can target a published race. A 2026 youth program used Tuesday evenings and county documents still list annual track passes.

name: Markham Park Mountain Bike Trails
cost: $5–$15; daily trail pass or membership, park entry extra when charged
dates: Year-round, daily until sunset; trail fee or annual membership required
customer: Mountain bikers, adaptive riders, off-road beginners
unique: Volunteer-maintained singletrack on the Everglades edge offers roughly 14 miles of rocky and rooty riding, including a separate approximately four-mile route for off-road hand-powered recumbent bikes and less experienced riders.
buzz: The roots and limestone make this more technical than the flat map suggests. The easier handcycle-compatible route broadens access, but riders still need the required daily pass or membership and must be off the trails by sunset.

name: Fox Observatory Public Night
dates: Year-round, Saturday after sunset, weather permitting; seasonal closing times
company: South Florida Amateur Astronomers Association at Markham Park
customer: Astronomy beginners, families, photographers, night-sky visitors
unique: Members of a club founded in 1965 open Markham Park's observatory and their telescopes to the public, letting visitors look at planets, the Moon and deep-sky objects with people who know the equipment.
buzz: The volunteer explanations are as useful as the telescope views, and no personal telescope is needed. Cloud cover cancels the value of the trip, and winter sessions end earlier than daylight-saving sessions.

name: Florida Panthers at Amerant Bank Arena
dates: Seasonal, generally October–April plus playoffs; published 2026–27 home schedule
company: Florida Panthers and Amerant Bank Arena
customer: Hockey fans, sports travelers, groups, couples
unique: South Florida's NHL team plays its home schedule in Sunrise, with theme nights, rivalry games and the arena's sightlines providing a live ice sport at the edge of the Everglades.
buzz: A rivalry or theme-night game adds to the atmosphere, but dynamically priced seats can move well above the low end of the range. The published 2026–27 calendar confirms an active home season rather than a touring exhibition.

name: Ski Rixen USA Cable Wakeboarding
dates: Year-round, Tuesday–Friday 2–7 p.m., weekends noon–7 p.m.; closed Monday; registered weekend lessons 10 a.m.–noon
company: Ski Rixen USA at Quiet Waters Park
customer: Wakeboard beginners, water-sports travelers, teenagers, active groups
unique: A full-size overhead cable more than 2,700 feet long pulls riders around a Quiet Waters lake without a boat, with beginner lessons, continuous laps and optional ramps and rails for experienced riders.
buzz: The basic two-hour pass includes ride time and some equipment, but wakeboard and obstacle-ready rentals cost more. Beginners should book the slower weekend lesson block instead of arriving during open riding and expecting instruction.

name: Deerfield Island Park
dates: Boat access only; free mainland shuttle Friday–Sunday hourly 10 a.m.–3 p.m.
customer: Walkers, birders, boaters, nature photographers
unique: Broward's only island park is a nature refuge on the Intracoastal Waterway at Hillsboro Boulevard, reachable by private boat or the county's free weekend shuttle rather than by a road entrance.
buzz: The boat crossing and lack of road access are the point. The shuttle operates only Friday through Sunday, and the 3 p.m. departure is the last hourly run, so this needs more timing than an ordinary county-park stop.

name: SS Copenhagen and Shipwreck Snorkel Trail
cost: Free self-guided; boat charter and rental gear extra
dates: Year-round in calm sea conditions; SS Copenhagen requires a boat
company: Town of Lauderdale-by-the-Sea and local dive charters
customer: Snorkelers, divers, maritime-history visitors, photographers
unique: The 1900 British steamer wreck rests in roughly 15–30 feet of water as a state underwater archaeological preserve, while a separate Datura Avenue snorkel trail and nearshore reefs offer a beach-accessible alternative.
buzz: Do not confuse the two sites. The Copenhagen is about three-quarters of a mile offshore and needs a boat and mooring buoy; the Datura trail is in about 10 feet of water. Visibility and surge determine whether either is worthwhile.

name: Lady Luck Wreck Dive
dates: Year-round on scheduled dive boats; advanced certification and sea conditions required
company: South Florida Diving Headquarters and Shipwreck Park Pompano Beach
customer: Advanced scuba divers, wreck photographers, artificial-reef students
unique: The 324-foot former New York sludge tanker Newtown Creek became the Lady Luck artificial reef in 2016, with Dennis McDonald's casino-themed octopus dealers, card sharks and slot machines installed on deck.
buzz: The underwater casino gives the wreck a specific visual identity beyond a rusting hull. Depths run roughly 60–130 feet, so this is an advanced boat dive, not a snorkel stop, and the standard charter price does not include a full gear package.

name: Sample-McDougald House
dates: Year-round, Tuesday–Saturday noon–4 p.m.; guided tours at noon, 1, 2 and 3 p.m.
customer: Historic-house visitors, local-history readers, architecture fans
unique: Pompano pioneer Albert Neal Sample's 1916 Georgian Revival farmhouse survives with both Sample and McDougald family furnishings after the 4,500-square-foot house was moved to Centennial Park in 2001.
buzz: The two-family story and the move explain how suburban Pompano consumed its farm landscape. The docent tour covers both floors in about 45 minutes, with foyer photographs available for visitors unable to use the stairs.

name: Cap's Place Island Restaurant
dates: Year-round dinner, Wednesday–Sunday from 5:30 p.m.; closed Monday and Tuesday
customer: Food-history travelers, seafood diners, couples, boaters
unique: A restaurant built on an old barge and reached by Cap's motor launch preserves its origins as the 1928 Club Unique, a Prohibition-era speakeasy, gambling spot and seafood house on a Lighthouse Point peninsula.
buzz: The launch, rough timber building and rum-running history are as much of the meal as the catch and hearts-of-palm salad. This is a dinner reservation, not a casual lunchtime stop, and hours can vary.

name: Butterfly World
dates: Year-round; Monday–Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; last entry 4 p.m.
customer: Families, gardeners, photographers, butterfly and bird visitors
unique: Screened tropical gardens at Tradewinds Park support thousands of flying butterflies and birds, with a lorikeet encounter and planted pathways that put visitors inside the enclosure rather than behind glass.
buzz: Arriving by midafternoon leaves enough time before the butterfly area closes at 4:30 p.m. Lorikeet nectar is a small separate cash purchase, and weather can alter operations, so this is not a rushed final stop of the day.

name: Tall Cypress Natural Area
dates: Year-round, daily sunrise to sunset
company: Broward County and City of Coral Springs
customer: Walkers, plant and bird visitors, families, photographers
unique: An elevated half-mile boardwalk crosses a preserved basin swamp and pine habitat inside suburban Coral Springs, with interpretive signs and close views into cypress forest without entering the wet ground.
buzz: The short boardwalk is the entire visit and works best as an early or late-hour nature stop. The city lists 68.36 acres, but the public walk samples only a compact portion, which keeps expectations in proportion.

name: Sawgrass Nature Center and Wildlife Hospital
dates: Year-round; Tuesday–Friday 9 a.m.–5 p.m., weekends 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; closed Monday
company: Sawgrass Nature Center and Wildlife Hospital
customer: Families, native-wildlife visitors, rehabilitation volunteers
unique: A small public nature center supports a working hospital for injured native wildlife, using resident animals and education programs to explain rehabilitation and release rather than presenting a conventional zoo.
buzz: The modest public exhibits and low admission are worth the stop if visitors understand the mission. The wildlife hospital itself is not open for tours because patient stress and safety take priority over spectacle.

name: Shiva Vishnu Temple of South Florida
dates: Year-round with split morning and evening hours; check festival calendar and worship etiquette
company: Shiva Vishnu Temple of South Florida
customer: Temple-architecture visitors, Hindu worshippers, art and religion students
unique: A traditional Dravidian temple designed under chief architect Ganapati Sthapati, with entrance and shrine towers, work by sculptors from Mahabalipuram and distinct Chola, Pandya, Vijayanagara and Kerala architectural references.
buzz: The carved forms and active ritual life make this a place of worship first and an architecture visit second. The temple closes between daily sessions on weekdays and weekends, so check hours and dress and photography expectations before entering.

name: Gulfstream Park Championship Meet
dates: Seasonal race meets; Championship Meet live racing Thursday–Sunday; Pegasus World Cup January 30, 2027
customer: Horse-racing visitors, sports groups, handicappers, event travelers
unique: Thoroughbred racing at the 1939 Hallandale track centers on the paddock, walking ring and stretch run, with the Championship Meet, Florida Derby and January Pegasus World Cup forming distinct levels of race-day visit.
buzz: An ordinary race afternoon is a different purchase from Pegasus or a packaged tasting event. Watch the horses in the walking ring before a race and check reserved-seat pricing, since marquee dates and hospitality packages cost much more.

name: Plantation Historical Museum
dates: Year-round, Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed Sunday–Tuesday
company: City of Plantation and Plantation Historical Society
customer: Local-history readers, families, school groups
unique: A volunteer-supported city museum on Fig Tree Lane concentrates on Plantation's development and community collections, offering a small-scale record of a suburb whose history is usually overlooked between Fort Lauderdale and Davie.
buzz: This is a short local stop rather than a regional destination museum. Visitors value the volunteer explanations and free admission, and pairing it with another Broward historical site makes a more substantial afternoon.
